newsitem.title: JAPAN: INTERVIEW - Shin-Etsu remains firm on U.S. PVC plant.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Shin-Etsu remains firm on U.S. PVC plant.

text.p: Shin-Etsu Chemical Co Ltd says it is sticking to its plan to build a 500,000 tonnes-per-year polyvinyl chloride resin (PVC) factory in the United States despite opposition from environmentalists.

"Although the start of operations will be delayed for around one year from the original schedule of the summer of 1998, we don't intend to change our plan (on the factory)," president Chihiro Kanagawa told Reuters in a recent interview.
The world's largest producer of PVC and silicon wafers plans to spend about $700 million to build its second U.S. factory for the production of PVC in the state of Louisiana.
However, the company has decided to suspend construction for now as environmental groups have been campaigning against the plant.
Kanagawa said that the suspension is expected to have a positive impact on the supply-and-demand condition in the PVC market.
He noted that PVC prices bottomed out in January and would continue to move in a relatively narrow range for a while. He said prices would begin to firm from the autumn.
"Considering market conditions, it may be a good thing that we suspended plant construction, although it is a negative factor for our company," said Kanagawa.

The Japanese financial daily Nihon Keizai Shimbun reported earlier this week that three of Japan's major PVC makers were moving to cut output by more than 10 percent to keep the market tight. Domestic PVC makers have been suffering from fierce competition due to an oversupply in the market.
Kanagawa said that sales of semiconductor wafers and other electronic devices have been unexpectedly favourable.

He also said the company plans group based capital investment of 450 to 600 billion yen in the five-year period to March 2001. The investments will be mainly in the areas of semiconductor wafers and optical fibre.

On ways to procure funds in the future, Shin-Etsu president said the company could choose equity financing, in addition to bank loans and corporate bond issues, as it has a relatively small number of issued shares.
